blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Conversational QA systems should fix errors when users push back and signal which answers to trust. We split each follow-up into its speech act (re-ask, agree, or challenge) and its payload (an answer string, correct or not), and measure four confidence signals on the same transcripts: verbalized confidence, length-normalized likelihood, a frozen hidden-state probe, and P(True). Answers change when the user supplies an answer string and almost never under the speech act alone: in every retained full-size cell, the correct answer converts at least four times as many wrong answers as re-asking or agreement. The four signals disagree. On Qwen2.5-7B the frozen probe rises with answer persistence rather than truth; this holds on held-out questions, with Llama-3-8B (cleaned answers) as support, but not on four other models. Among 81 Qwen2.5-7B errors that survive one re-ask, re-asking, a fresh chat, or abstain repair almost none, while a gold answer repairs 75-95%. In two preregistered replications, every repair rate without an answer string stays below 0.15; a larger post-hoc rerun excludes 0.15 except for the empty elicit. With BM25 TriviaQA evidence, sentences that contain the answer repair 67-76% of persistent errors versus at most 12% when they do not. An end-to-end contain-gate cuts harm on TriviaQA, but a deployable gate that does not know the gold answer repairs few errors.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Chat assistants built on large language models (LLMs) now answer questions in customer support, tutoring, search, and clinical or legal help lines. There, a wrong answer costs something. Two questions follow, both about the reliability of conversational QA and evidence retrieval under user feedback. When a user pushes back, does the system fix its errors or just change its mind? And can the system’s own confidence tell the operator which answers to trust? Recent work on the second question asks whether LLM confidence stays calibrated as a conversation goes on Zhang
et al. (2026a) ; Zhang et al. (2026b) . These studies usually score one confidence measure (verbalized confidence, the self-evaluation probability P ⁡ ( True ) P(\mathrm{True}) , or sequence likelihood) against correctness, as if each were an estimate of the same underlying belief.

blocks.en: For that to work, the measures must move together, and every follow-up must count as the same kind of evidence. In our data, neither holds. So we ask a simpler question: when a user sends a follow-up message, which quantity does it change? Figure 1 summarizes the answer. We split each follow-up into two parts. The speech act is what the user does: re-ask, agree, or say the model is wrong. The payload is an optional answer string in the message, either the correct (“gold”) answer or a plausible wrong one (a “foil”). Payloads change the model’s answer. Speech acts alone almost never repair an error. Changes to the answer, whether or not the new answer is true, move a frozen probe readout that, on Qwen2.5-7B, goes with answer persistence. We call it the persistence readout s t s_{t} and make no psychological or causal claim about it. The other measures respond to other things: verbalized confidence to the number of turns, sequence likelihood to how fluently the model repeats itself, and P ⁡ ( True ) P(\mathrm{True}) to explicit contradiction. Two papers that calibrate different measures and call both “confidence” are not reporting comparable numbers.

blocks.en: We offer a map of interventions and their effects, not a new method: 1. The answer string, not the speech act, moves the answer. Answers follow a stated gold or foil string. Re-asking and agreement do not repair errors (Section 4 ). 2. The measures come apart across turns. Single-turn work has shown that verbalized confidence and correctness-tracking signals are not interchangeable Kumaran (2026) ; Miao and Ungar (2026) . We show the same split in dialogue for four measures (verbalized confidence, likelihood, a frozen hidden-state probe, and P ⁡ ( True ) P(\mathrm{True}) ), in raw scores and in calibration error, and we show which part of the user turn each one responds to (Section 5 ). 3. On Qwen2.5-7B the frozen probe goes with answer persistence, and persistent errors are hard to undo. The persistence readout s t = σ ⁡ ( v acc ⊤ ​ h ~ t ) s_{t}=\sigma(v_{\mathrm{acc}}^{\top}\tilde{h}_{t}) is a frozen probe on the current answer state (Section 3.4 ). On Qwen2.5-7B it rises on stay-wrong items and on I → \to C items, also on held-out questions and above a shuffled-label control. Llama-3-8B with cut answers supports this; on the other four models it does not hold on held-out questions. Resetting the chat or offering abstention does not recover these errors; a gold string at turn 3 does (Section 6.1 ). 4. A retrieval heuristic. Before relying on evidence to repair an answer, check that it contains the answer string. This is a hypothesis for system design, not a validated rule. Across four models, a retrieved sentence without it repairs at most 0.16 0.16 of stay-wrong items under any of our scorers, and it breaks up to 0.70 0.70 of correct answers (Section 6.1 ). The first three points share one argument: if two measures respond to different controlled interventions and disagree on the same transcript, they cannot both estimate a single latent conversational confidence. We do not propose a new uncertainty estimator. Section 8 lists what we do not claim.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Instruction-tuned LLMs tend to adopt a view the user states, even when it is wrong. Perez et al. (2023) documented this with model-written evaluations and found that it grows with model size and with reinforcement learning from human feedback. Sharma et al. (2024) showed that sycophancy is common across production assistants and traced it partly to human preference judgments that reward agreement. Wei et al. (2023) found that scaling and instruction tuning increase sycophancy, that models agree with a user’s clearly false arithmetic claims, and that fine-tuning on simple synthetic data reduces it. These works show that a user’s stated answer is persuasive. They usually bundle the stance (“I think you are wrong”) with the stated string. Our factorial design separates the two. For short factual answers, the string does almost all of the work.
blocks.zh: 指令调制LLMs倾向于采用用户表示的视图,即使它是错误的. 佩雷斯等编. (2023年)用模型写作的评价记录了这一点,并发现它随着模型的大小和从人类反馈中学习的强化而增长. Sharma等人(2024年)表明,在生产助理中节奏很常见,并部分追溯到奖励协议的人类偏好判断. Wei等 (2023年)发现,缩放和指令调制增加了节能,模型同意用户明显虚假的算术主张,而对简单的合成数据的微调则会减少. 这些作品表明,用户所陈述的答案是令人信服的。 他们通常将姿态(“我认为你错了”)与指定的字符串捆绑在一起。 我们的元素设计将两者分开. 对于简短的事实答案,弦几乎全部完成.

blocks.en: Other work studies what happens when a user challenges an answer, with or without offering a new one. In the FlipFlop experiment, Laban et al. (2023) showed that a simple “Are you sure?” makes models change their answers and lowers accuracy. Xie et al. (2024) found that models waver under skeptical, negating, or misleading follow-ups even when the first answer was correct, and proposed a training method to reduce this. Wang et al. (2023) showed that ChatGPT often cannot defend a correct answer against invalid arguments. Huang et al. (2024) found that models rarely improve their reasoning by intrinsic self-correction without outside feedback, and Laban et al. (2026) showed that performance drops across many tasks in multi-turn conversation. Our results agree on one side and add the other: empty challenges break correct answers (C → \to I), but neither challenges nor re-asks repair wrong ones (I → \to C). We also test whether a persistent error survives a chat reset.
blocks.zh: 其他工作研究了当一个用户质疑一个答案时会发生什么,是否有新的答案。 在FlipFlop实验中,Laban等人(2023年)表明,一个简单的“你确定吗?”使模型改变答案并降低准确度。 谢等 (2024年)发现模型在怀疑,否定,或误导后继的情况下,即使第一个答案正确,也会产生动摇,并提出了减少这种情况的训练方法. Wang等(2023年)显示,ChatGPT往往无法针对无效论点为正确的答案辩护. Huang等 (2024)发现模型很少通过内在的自我校正来改进推理,没有外界的反馈,而Laban等 (2026)在多回合对话中显示性能会跨越许多任务. 我们的结果一方面是一致的,另一方面是补充:空洞的挑战打破了正确的答案(C-~~~到一),但无论是挑战还是重新任务都不修复错误的答案(I-~~到C). 我们还测试一个持续错误是否在聊天重置后存活.

blocks.en: Asking a model to state its confidence is the cheapest measure in deployed systems. Lin et al. (2022) showed that a fine-tuned GPT-3 can express calibrated uncertainty in words. Without such fine-tuning, the stated confidence of instruction-tuned models is often overconfident or poorly calibrated Xiong et al. (2024) , though prompting can help, especially for models trained with human feedback Tian et al. (2023) . Geng et al. (2024) survey confidence estimation and calibration for LLMs. Calibration is usually measured with ECE Guo et al. (2017) . In our dialogues, the movement of verbalized confidence is mostly a Qwen2.5-7B effect of turn depth, not a response to evidence.
blocks.zh: 要求一个模型说明其信心是部署系统中最便宜的衡量标准。 Lin等 (2022年)显示,经过微调的GPT-3可以用文字表达校正的不确定性. 没有这种微调,指示调试模型的所宣称的信心往往过于自信或校准差的Xiong等人(2024年),尽管催化可以有所帮助,特别是对于经过人类反馈培训的模型Tian等人(2023年). 耿等编. (2024) 调查LLMs的信心估计和校正。 校正通常用ECE Guo等人(2017年)测量. 在我们的对话中,口语化的信心运动主要是转弯深度的Quen2.5-7B效应,而不是对证据的反应.

blocks.en: Kadavath et al. (2022) asked a model whether its own proposed answer is true and read the probability of “True”. They found this fairly well calibrated for large models on many single-turn tasks. In our dialogues P ⁡ ( True ) P(\mathrm{True}) ranks correct answers well at both turns but barely moves under re-asking or agreement. It responds mainly to contradiction by a foil.
blocks.zh: Kadavath等人(2022年)询问一个模型,它自己提出的答案是否正确,并读取“True”的概率。 他们发现这相当适合许多单回合任务的大型模型。 在我们的对话中, P (真) P (\ mathrm{ True}) 在两个回合中正确回答, 但很少在重新任务或协议下移动 。 它主要对一个被挫败的矛盾作出反应.

blocks.en:
Several papers train classifiers on hidden activations to read out whether a statement or answer is true. Azaria and
Mitchell (2023) trained such a classifier on true and false statements. Marks and Tegmark (2024) reported linear structure that separates true from false statements. Burns et al. (2023) found latent knowledge without labels. Orgad et al. (2025) showed that truthfulness signals concentrate in the exact answer tokens, generalize poorly across datasets, and that a model may encode the correct answer while generating a wrong one. A probe can learn the task itself rather than reveal what the representation encodes, so probe results need care Hewitt and Liang (2019) . We fit a probe at turn 1, freeze it, and follow it after the user speaks again.
blocks.zh:
一些论文在隐藏活化器上训练分类器,以读出一个陈述或答案是否真实. 阿扎里亚和
米切尔(2023年)在真实和虚假的陈述上训练了这样一个分类员. Marks和Tegmark (2024)报告了线性结构,将真实与虚假陈述区分开来. Burns等人(2023年)发现了没有标签的潜在知识。 Orgad等人(2025年)表明,真实性信号集中在准确的答案符上,对数据集的概括性差,一个模型可能在生成错误答案的同时编码正确答案. 探险者可以了解任务本身,而不是揭示什么代表编码,因此探险结果需要注意Hewitt和Liang (2019). 我们装了个探测器 在一号弯,冻结它,然后在用户再次说话后跟踪它。

blocks.en: Two recent single-turn studies are close to our result on the measures. Kumaran (2026) used a two-stage task: a model answers and reports its confidence, then later decides whether to give the answer to a user or abstain. Across several models, verbal confidence predicted the later commit-or-abstain decision better than it predicted correctness, while calibrated token log-probabilities tracked correctness. In Gemma models, a post-answer hidden state encoded the later decision, and steering along a direction specific to verbal confidence shifted abstention. Miao and Ungar (2026) found that a linear accuracy probe and the direction behind verbalized confidence are nearly orthogonal, and used activation steering to bring verbalized confidence closer to the probe. We do not claim these points as new. Our study differs in three ways. The user turn is controlled, so we can separate the speech act from the answer string. The probe is fitted at turn 1 and frozen, and we follow the same items across turns. And we study the frozen probe readout, not verbalized confidence: in our dialogues, on Qwen2.5-7B, it is the probe that moves with the answer the model keeps. We run no steering, so unlike these two studies our evidence is correlational. Sarkar et al. (2026) show, in a collaborative dialogue task between two LLMs, that a partner’s assertion can shift a model’s linear representation of whether a proposition is true. Our probe result points the same way for short factual answers.
blocks.zh: 最近的两项单回合研究接近于我们有关这些措施的结果。 库马兰(2026年)采用分两个阶段的任务:一个模型答案并报告其信心,再后决定是给用户答案还是弃权. 在若干模型中,口头信任比预测正确性更能预测后来的承诺性或吸收性决定,同时校正符号概率跟踪正确性。 在Gemma模型中,一个后答后隐藏状态编码了后来的决定,并沿着口头信任的特定方向转向弃权. Miao和Ungar (2026年)发现线性精度探测器和口语化信心背后的方向接近正交,并使用活化向导使口语化信心更接近探测器. 我们并不认为这些观点是新的。 我们的研究在三个方面有所不同。 用户转弯被控制,因此我们可以将语音行为与回答字符串区分开来. 探测器安装在一号站台并被冷冻,我们沿着相同的物品穿过站台。 我们研究冷冻探测器的读取,而不是口头化的信心: 在我们的对话中,在Quen2.5-7B上,是探测器用模型保存的答案移动。 我们没有方向,所以不像这两个研究 我们的证据是相关的。 Sarkar等人(2026年)在两个LLMs之间的合作对话任务中表明,一个伙伴的断言可以改变模型对一个命题是否真实的线性表述. 我们的探测结果对简短的事实答案同样如此。

blocks.en:
The closest work studies confidence across turns. Zhang
et al. (2026a) evaluate verbalized confidence, P ⁡ ( True ) P(\mathrm{True}) , and a new P ⁡ ( Sufficient ) P(\mathrm{Sufficient}) score as hints accumulate, and propose an information-aware ECE (InfoECE) that requires confidence to rise steadily as gold information arrives. Zhang et al. (2026b) show that persuasion worsens a turn-level ECE (ECE@T) and that sequence likelihood can rise when the answer flips to a wrong one, and they train a calibrator, MTCal, to repair the score. Both ask how well a score tracks correctness. We use their setting (short-answer dialogue under persuasion) and ask an earlier question: which quantity a given user turn moves (Table 1 ).
blocks.zh:
最接近的工作研究 信心跨转。 张
等 (2026a) 评估口语化的自信, P (真) P (\ mathrm{ True}), 和一个新的 P (足够) P (\ mathrm{ 足够) 积分作为提示, 并提议一个信息化的 ECE (InfoECE), 需要信心随着黄金信息的到来而稳步上升. Zhang等 (2026b) 显示劝说使一个转弯级的ECE(ECE@T)恶化,当答案翻到一个错误时序列概率会上升,他们训练出一个计算器MTCal来修复分数. 都问分数正确性有多好 我们使用它们的设置(在说服下进行短答对话),并询问一个更早的问题:给定的用户转动的数量(表1).

blocks.en: Models follow context that contradicts their stored knowledge to varying degrees Longpre et al. (2021) ; Xie et al. (2024) , and whether retrieved context is sufficient to answer the question predicts errors in retrieval-augmented generation Joren et al. (2025) . Lathkar (2026) reports that, in multi-hop retrieval-augmented QA, one confirmed intermediate fact can raise the rate of confident wrong answers before complete evidence lowers it. That work is single-turn and measures confidence; we measure whether evidence repairs an error that has already survived a re-ask. In our data, evidence repairs such an error only when it contains the answer string.
blocks.zh: 模型遵循的上下文不同程度地与所存储的知识相矛盾 Longpre等 (2021); Xie等 (2024) ,以及检索到的上下文是否足以回答问题,预言了被检索到的一代Joren等 (2025) 中的错误. Lathkar (2026)报道说,在多跳回取增强QA中,一个确认的中间事实可以提高自信错误答案的速率而后再被完整证据降低. 这项工作是一次性的,并衡量信心;我们衡量证据修复工作是否是一个已经幸存下来的错误。 在我们的数据中,只有在包含答案字符串时,证据才会修复这样的错误.

blocks.en: 3.4 The persistence readout: an operational definition
blocks.zh: 3.4 国家 持久性读取:业务定义

blocks.en: Let h t ∈ ℝ d h_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} be the last-layer hidden state averaged (mean-pooled) over the answer tokens at turn t t , and let h ~ t \tilde{h}_{t} be h t h_{t} standardized with the training-set mean and variance. We fit a weight vector v acc ∈ ℝ d v_{\mathrm{acc}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} by logistic regression to predict T1 correctness from h 1 h_{1} , using only the unique persist T1 items of that model × \times dataset. GroupKFold cross-validation is used only as a sanity check. We then freeze v acc v_{\mathrm{acc}} and never refit it after the user speaks. The persistence readout at turn t t is s t = σ ⁡ ( v acc ⊤ ​ h ~ t ) , s_{t}\;=\;\sigma\!\bigl(v_{\mathrm{acc}}^{\top}\tilde{h}_{t}\bigr), (1) where σ ⁡ ( x ) = 1 / ( 1 + e − x ) \sigma(x)=1/(1+e^{-x}) is the logistic function. We use “probe” and s t s_{t} interchangeably and write Δ ​ s = s 2 − s 1 \Delta s=s_{2}-s_{1} . Three points make the definition precise: • What it is. s t s_{t} is a frozen readout of the current answer state. The linear map is one choice. Our claims about s t s_{t} apply to any frozen readout that is fitted only on unique T1 states, is not refitted after the user speaks, and rises on stay-wrong and on I → \to C items (Section 6 ). • What the name means. “Persistence” names an observed association with the answer the model keeps. We make no claim about a psychological state, and no claim that s t s_{t} causes the answer. The main analyses fit the probe on unique T1 items and apply it to rows of the same questions. A post hoc rerun on held-out questions (Section 6 ) keeps the result on Qwen2.5-7B only. • Why it is not truth. If s t s_{t} measured truth, it would rise only when the answer becomes gold. Instead it rises on stay-wrong and on I → \to C items and falls on C → \to I items. • The behaviour it goes with. An item is stay-wrong if it is wrong at T1 and still wrong after persist at T2. On Qwen2.5-7B TriviaQA there are n = 81 n{=}81 such items, and Δ ​ s > 0 \Delta s>0 on 79 of their 80 distinct questions. blocks.en: Answers are normalized (lowercased, articles removed, whitespace collapsed) and counted correct on an exact match or on whole-word containment, in either direction, between the answer and a gold alias Joshi et al. (2017) . We call this the contain matcher. It is the primary, preregistered scorer. Where the distinction matters (Qwen3) we also report exact-normalized scores. Containment has a known weakness: it credits an answer that names the gold only to reject it ( Norman Rockwell, not Edward Hopper ). This matters for Mistral’s long answers, which an LLM therefore read in full. Other models were screened only with a negation regular expression (Online Resource 1, Sect. I). The second preregistration also scored every answer with an LLM judge. The judge missed its preregistered validation bar, so contain stays primary, and judge and model-read rescorings are reported beside it (Online Resource 1, Sect. H). Post hoc, two independent people labelled a blind sample of 300 300 V2 rows; on the 272 272 clear ENDORSES/DOES_NOT pairs Cohen’s κ \kappa was 0.86 0.86 (agreement 253 / 272 253/272 ), with disagreements resolved by discussion. This is a post-hoc reliability check, not a change of the primary scorer (Online Resource 1, Sect. H).

blocks.en: Before any generation, a frozen pilot preregistration Tran (2026a) fixed two hypotheses and a stopping rule. H1 stated that the frozen v acc v_{\mathrm{acc}} predicts T2 correctness after misleading persuasion better than verbalized confidence does. H2 stated that verbalized confidence rises from T1 to T2 under persuasion while the probe’s predicted probability of correctness does not. H2 failed its gate: verbalized confidence fell ( − 0.17 -0.17 ). H1 met neither preregistered bar: the advantage was + 0.06 +0.06 with a bootstrap interval covering zero. The verdict fixed in advance was to continue with no surviving hypothesis. We report H2 as failed rather than dropping it. What replaced the hypotheses was an observation: the measures were responding to different parts of the user’s turn.
blocks.zh: 在任何一代人之前,一个被冻结的飞行员预注册Tran (2026a)固定了两个假设和一个停止规则. H1表示被冻结的 v cc v_{\ mathrm{acc}}} 预言T2在误导劝导后比口语化的自信更正确. H2表示,在说服下,口语化的信心从T1上升到了T2,而探测器的预测正确概率却并非如此. H2故障出门:口语化信心下降(−0.17-0.17. H1既未遇到预先注册的栏杆:优势是+0.06+0.06,靴子间隔为0. 事先确定的判决是,在没有存续假设的情况下继续进行。 我们报告H2失败了,而不是放弃它。 取代这些假设的是观察:这些措施是针对用户转向的不同部分。

blocks.en: Apart from two later preregistered studies of persistent errors and retrieval Tran (2026b) ; Tran (2026c) (Section 6.1 ), nothing in this paper is confirmatory. blocks.en: The probe’s own drop in AUROC ( 0.848 → 0.649 0.848\to 0.649 ) is not noise. It is the persistence effect of Section 6 seen in calibration terms. A readout that rises on items that stay wrong (Table 4 ) must lose discrimination against correctness once the user has spoken, because it now follows the answer the model keeps rather than what is true. In the same turn, the probe becomes a worse readout of truth and a better readout of answer persistence, and a single “confidence” number hides this.

blocks.en: A re-ask, a chat reset, or an abstain option will not undo a persistent error, and a drop in verbalized confidence will not flag one. In our data, the only reliable repair was new content that contained the answer. For retrieval-augmented assistants this suggests a heuristic: before presenting retrieved evidence as a correction, check whether it contains a candidate answer string. In our data, evidence without one rarely repairs an error and can break up to 0.70 0.70 of answers that were correct. In a post hoc end-to-end test (BM25 passages, TriviaQA and HotpotQA, three models; Online Resource 1, Table J12), the gold-based gate cut harm on TriviaQA while keeping most repairs (Llama, k = 1 k=1 : harm 0.179 → 0.038 0.179\to 0.038 , net per 100 items 15.9 → 27.4 15.9\to 27.4 ); on HotpotQA the gain was mixed. A gate that checks the model’s own answer instead of the gold repaired only 0.02 0.02 – 0.12 0.12 of errors, and dense retrieval and a judge check were not run. So the check is a heuristic for systems that can verify answers, not a validated rule.
blocks.zh: 重置任务,聊天重置,或弃权选项不会消除持续错误,而口语化信心的下降也不会标出一个. 在我们的数据中,唯一可靠的修复就是包含答案的新内容。 对于检索辅助人员来说,这意味着一种休克主义:在提出取回的证据作为更正之前,检查它是否包含一个候选的回答字符串。 在我们的数据中,没有证据的证据很少修复一个错误,并且可以破解到0.700.70的正确答案. 在一次后期端到端试验(BM25通道,TriviaQA和HotpotQA三种型号;在线资源1,表J12)中,以金为基的门在保持大部分修理的同时将TriviaQA的伤害切除(Llama,k=1k=1:伤害0.179~0.038 0.179~0.038,每100个项目净值为15.9~27.4 15.9~27.4);在HotpotQA上,收益褒贬不一. 一个检查模型本身答案而不是金子的门只修复了0.02 0.02 – 0.12 0.12个出错,密集检索和法官检查没有运行. 因此,该检查对于能够验证答案的系统来说是一种heuristic,而不是经过验证的规则.

blocks.en: 8 Limitations
blocks.zh: 8 限制

blocks.en:
We do not claim that verbalized confidence always falls over turns (we observe this for Qwen2.5-7B only), that hidden states contain a truth direction, or that we outperform MTCal Zhang et al. (2026b) or P ⁡ ( Sufficient ) P(\mathrm{Sufficient}) Zhang
et al. (2026a) on ECE. We do not claim to be first to show that verbalized confidence and correctness-tracking signals come apart, or that confidence can track commitment; single-turn studies showed both Kumaran (2026) ; Miao and Ungar (2026) . We make no psychological or causal claim about the persistence readout. We propose no new uncertainty estimator.

blocks.en: All experiments use English short-answer question answering, with GSM8K run under the same short-answer protocol. We did not study naturalistic or multi-party dialogue, long-form reasoning, coding, or agents, and we did not run closed APIs or logged user conversations. Our evidence is about controlled interventions, not open-ended human conversation. The turn-3 battery contains no reasoning prompt, so we do not claim that step-by-step reconsideration cannot repair persistent errors. The factorial design is not a formal causal-identification argument.

blocks.en: 9 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 9 结论

blocks.en: In short-answer question answering, an LLM’s confidence in a conversation is not one belief waiting for a better estimator. What the user supplies (an answer string) moves the answer. How the user phrases the turn (re-asking, agreeing, or accusing) does not. Four common confidence measures respond to different parts of the same turn, and on Qwen2.5-7B a frozen hidden-state readout follows the answer the model keeps rather than its truth. Errors that survive one re-ask are not undone by re-asking, resetting, or offering abstention. A correct answer string repairs them, including one inside real retrieved evidence. For practitioners our data suggest a heuristic that still needs end-to-end testing: before relying on evidence to correct a model, check that it contains the answer.
blocks.zh: 在简短的回答问题时,LLM对对话的信心并不是一种等待更好的估计者的信念。 用户提供什么(一个答案字符串)来移动答案. 用户的短语(重新询问、同意或指责)如何不会。 四个共同的建立信任措施对同一转弯的不同部分作出反应,在Quen2.5-7B上,一个被冻结的隐藏状态读取遵循了模型所保存的答案而不是其真实性. 在重新任务中幸存的错误不会通过重新任务、重新设定或弃权来弥补。 一个正确的答案字符串修复它们, 包括一个内部 真实取出的证据。 对于从业者来说,我们的数据表明一种需要端到端测试的热度:在依赖证据纠正模型之前,检查它是否包含答案.
